row.team_price_text: Standard: $49.90/mo for 1 connection, up to 20 users (billed annually)
row.evidence: AnyDesk's help centre lists three user provider options in my.anydesk II (Admin, IDP via OpenID Connect, and LDAP), all Ultimate-Cloud; no SCIM endpoint is documented on the pricing page, the help-centre index or the REST API page.
row.notes: Status changed from June 'partial' to 'none' (by absence, confidence medium). June said SCIM required Ultimate, but no first-party page mentions SCIM: the help-centre sitemap and llms.txt index have no SCIM article, and the pricing comparison has no SCIM row. Ultimate (Contact Sales, from 5 licensed users) offers SSO through an OpenID Connect 'IDP' user provider, which creates and syncs users from the IdP at sign-in, and an LDAP user provider; those are recorded as fallbacks. Prices changed since June: Solo is now $28.90/mo (was $14.90); Standard $49.90/mo and Advanced $111.90/mo are unchanged; all plans are billed yearly and the monthly figures are the annual equivalent (a 20% first-year discount is advertised). Licensing is per concurrent connection, so per-user fields are null. Team plan switched from Solo to Standard because Solo is a single-user licence. The my.anydesk I REST API (Standard and up) covers licences, clients, sessions and address books, not users.

scim.notes: No SCIM documentation found; the vendor never says 'no', so available stays null and status is 'none' by absence.

auth.notes: License ID plus API password requested from AnyDesk support.

limitations.text: The REST API (Standard, Advanced, Ultimate-Cloud, On-Premises) lists licence, account, client, session and address-book commands only; full endpoint docs sit in the logged-in my.anydesk Files tab.

user_api.notes: available=false because the REST API page enumerates every supported command and none manages users.

okta.notes: OIN search for 'anydesk' returns no results.

entra.notes: anydesk-tutorial and anydesk-provisioning-tutorial on learn.microsoft.com return 404; AnyDesk's IDP guide uses Azure AD only as a generic OpenID Connect example.

fallbacks.other_sync: LDAP user provider (Microsoft Active Directory, OpenLDAP, OpenDJ) for sign-in and LDAP role import; Ultimate-Cloud
fallbacks.notes: The OIDC 'IDP' user provider creates users through the IdP and keeps them synchronized from it; the docs do not describe deprovisioning.
